description: What servers can send to the internet. A web server with a public IP leaves through the internet gateway as itself. Servers in a private subnet leave through a NAT gateway as its Elastic IP, and only when the NAT gateway's subnet routes to the internet gateway and every network ACL on the way allows the traffic out and the replies back, on the server's ephemeral ports and the NAT gateway's own. A database that can send anything anywhere is an exfiltration path. A server whose subnet routes to the internet gateway but has no public IP cannot reach the internet; a subnet with only the local route cannot either.
